9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: medium wide, slightly above, Scarlett (Image 2) begins descending the stairs with one hand near the black rail, her phone secured and lipstick tucked away., Scarlett (Image 2) moves diagonally through the concrete stairwell, black rail leading toward her and sunlit landings creating alternating bands of light across her face., apartment_hallway, Soft-to-moderate natural daylight enters from the building's windows or distant exit, producing an even corridor illumination rather than dramatic contrast., Warm cream walls, muted white and gray radiator metal, dark clothing, natural canvas, and vivid coral accents., Scarlett (Image 2), Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
